name: MonarchPasswordInput
title: PasswordInput
summary: A labelled password field with a toggle that shows the password as text, and the autofill content type for a current or a new password.
whenToUse: For a password or another secret the user types: sign-in, sign-up, password reset, confirming an action.
whenNotToUse: For a one-time code use MonarchOtpPinInput. For text that is not secret use MonarchTextField.
api: @Composable fun MonarchPasswordInput(value: String, onValueChange: (String) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, label: String? = null, placeholder: String? = null, helperText: String? = null, errorText: String? = null, purpose: MonarchPasswordInputPurpose = MonarchPasswordInputPurpose.Current, enabled: Boolean = true, revealed: Boolean? = null, onRevealedChange: ((Boolean) -> Unit)? = null, revealIcon: (@Composable (revealed: Boolean) -> Unit)? = null, keyboardActions: KeyboardActions = KeyboardActions.Default, labels: MonarchPasswordInputLabels = MonarchPasswordInputLabels(), interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null)
class MonarchPasswordInputLabels(reveal: String? = null, show: String? = null, hide: String? = null)

options.name: label
options.description: The visible label; it floats into the outline.

options.name: placeholder
options.description: Shown while the field is empty and focused.

options.name: errorText
options.description: When not null the field is in the error state and this replaces the helper text.

options.name: purpose
options.description: Current sets the Password autofill content type; New sets NewPassword, so the password manager offers to generate and save one.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the field and the toggle can be used.

options.name: revealed
options.description: Whether the password is shown as text. Null lets the field keep the state itself, starting hidden and surviving configuration changes.

options.name: onRevealedChange
options.description: Called with the new state when the toggle is used.

options.name: revealIcon
options.description: Replaces the text of the toggle, for example with an eye icon. Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: keyboardActions
options.description: What the IME action does, for example submit the form.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings: reveal ("Show password"), show ("Show"), hide ("Hide").

options.name: interactionSource
options.description: The source of the focus and press interactions of the field.

states.name: hidden
states.description: The text is drawn as dots and the toggle reads "Show".

states.name: revealed
states.description: The text is drawn as typed and the toggle reads "Hide".

states.name: focused
states.description: The outline takes the focus ring color, as in MonarchTextField.

states.name: error
states.description: A danger outline and the error message under the field in place of the helper text.

states.name: disabled
states.description: The subtle background and the disabled text color; the toggle is disabled too.

appearance: The field is MonarchTextField: a surface fill with the input border, the focus ring color when focused and the danger strong color in error. The toggle text uses the accent strong color, or the disabled text color when disabled, with the label type style. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web warns while Caps Lock is on; a touch keyboard has no Caps Lock state to read, so the warning is dropped, as on iOS. The web has sm, md and lg sizes; Android has the one size of MonarchTextField. iOS draws an eye symbol on the toggle; Monarch for Android bundles no icons, so the toggle shows the words Show and Hide unless the app passes revealIcon. The web's autocomplete current-password and new-password are the Compose autofill content types Password and NewPassword. iOS swaps a SecureField for a TextField, so VoiceOver reads a revealed password; Compose 1.12 does not update the password flag of an existing text field (CoreTextFieldSemanticsModifierNode.updateNodeSemantics never stores it), so TalkBack keeps treating the field as a password, and recreating the field would move TalkBack focus off the toggle. The reveal state is either hoisted (revealed with onRevealedChange) or kept by the field, as the web's controlled and uncontrolled forms.
accessibility: The field is the Material 3 text field with the password keyboard: TalkBack reads the label and the error and treats the text as a password. Compose 1.12 keeps the password flag of a text field from its first composition, so a field that starts hidden stays a password field for TalkBack after the toggle is used; the drawn text does change.
The toggle has the Checkbox role, the spoken name "Show password" in both states, and is read as on or off; its visible Show or Hide text is hidden from TalkBack so the name does not change.
The toggle reserves a touch target of at least 48dp by 48dp and draws the Monarch focus ring.
A disabled field also disables the toggle, which then ignores taps.
The autofill content type is Password or NewPassword, so password managers fill or generate the password.
The error is a message as well as a danger outline, not color alone.
edgeCases: A long toggle text at font scale 2.0 takes width from the text area of the field; keep the replacement short or use revealIcon.
Passing revealed without onRevealedChange makes the toggle report changes nobody stores, so it does not change.
The keyboard is the password keyboard without suggestions in both states.

examples.title: Sign in
examples.template:
MonarchPasswordInput(
    value = password,
    onValueChange = { password = it },
    label = {{label}},
    helperText = {{description}},
    purpose = MonarchPasswordInputPurpose.{{purpose|pascal}},
)
examples.code:
MonarchPasswordInput(
    value = password,
    onValueChange = { password = it },
    label = "Password",
    helperText = "The password for your account.",
    purpose = MonarchPasswordInputPurpose.Current,
)

examples.title: Sign up, with an error
examples.code:
MonarchPasswordInput(
    value = password,
    onValueChange = { password = it },
    label = "New password",
    purpose = MonarchPasswordInputPurpose.New,
    helperText = "At least 8 characters.",
    errorText = if (password.isNotEmpty() && password.length < 8) "Use at least 8 characters." else null,
)

examples.title: An eye icon on the toggle
examples.code:
MonarchPasswordInput(
    value = password,
    onValueChange = { password = it },
    label = "Password",
    revealIcon = { revealed ->
        Icon(
            imageVector = if (revealed) SampleIcons.EyeOff else SampleIcons.Eye,
            contentDescription = null,
        )
    },
)
